cohort: Fourteen patients who had undergone an unscheduled cesarean birth during labor and volunteered for the study.
finding: Four key themes emerged as contributors to patient dissatisfaction with unplanned cesarean births: poor communication, fear of the operating room, distrust of the medical team, and loss of control.
mod_finding: The identified factors (poor communication, fear, distrust, loss of control) related to the experience of unplanned cesarean birth suggest that changes in physician behavior regarding this mode of birth could reduce patient dissatisfaction.
cross-section timing: Interviews conducted between 2 and 6 weeks postpartum
